kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-01.prompt: A mushroom grows every day. For five days Maria took a picture of this mushroom, but she put the photos in the wrong order, as shown. Which sequence of photos correctly shows the mushroom growing, from left to right?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-02.prompt: Which of the tiles below is NOT part of the wall shown?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-03.prompt: John paints the squares of the board shown whose calculation gives 24. What does the painted board look like?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-04.prompt: Which of the following pictures can you NOT make using all the pieces shown?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-05.prompt: Eli drew a board with nine squares on the floor and wrote a number in each of them, starting with 1 and adding 3 to get each new number, until he filled the board. The picture shows three of the numbers that Eli wrote. Which number below could be the number in the coloured square?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-06.prompt: Paulo took a rectangular sheet of paper, yellow on one side and green on the other, and with several folds along the dotted lines in the figure he made a paper plane. Then Paulo made a round hole in it, marked in the last picture. After playing a lot with the plane, Paulo unfolded the sheet and saw several holes in it. How many holes did he count?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-07.prompt: Five children had to colour three quarters of the small squares on their trays. One of the children A, B, C, D or E made a mistake. Which one?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-08.prompt: Gaspar has these seven different pieces made of equal small squares. He uses all the pieces to build rectangles with different perimeters, that is, with different shapes. How many different perimeters can he get?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-09.prompt: Janaína made the construction shown on a grid, using some light cubes and some dark cubes. Looking at the construction from above, what does she see?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-10.prompt: Cynthia paints each region of the figure in a single colour: red, blue or yellow. Regions that touch each other must get different colours. In how many different ways can Cynthia paint the figure?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-11.prompt: Denis ties his dog with an 11-metre rope at a point one metre away from a corner of a fenced area about 7 metres by 5 metres, as shown. Denis places 5 bones near the fence, as shown in the picture. How many bones can the dog reach?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-12.prompt: Luana builds a fence using pieces of wood 2 metres long and half a metre wide. The picture shows the finished fence. How long is the fence, in metres?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-13.prompt: Amelia built a crown using 10 copies of the piece shown (a pentagon made of five triangles numbered 1 to 5). The pieces were joined so that sides in contact have the same number, as shown in the picture, where four pieces are visible. What number is in the coloured triangle?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-14.prompt: Julia drew the picture shown on a piece of cardboard, cut it out, folded it and glued it to form a cube. Which of the cubes below can be the one she made?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-15.prompt: Whenever the kangaroo goes up seven steps, the rabbit goes down three steps. When the kangaroo is on step number 56, on which step will the rabbit be?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-16.prompt: Ana, Bia and Cris have 100 reais together. They go to the movies and each one pays her own ticket. Before paying, Ana had twice as much as each of her friends. Now Ana has three times as much as her two friends together. How much did a movie ticket cost?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-17.prompt: The left cactus has three flowers on its back side. In total, the cactus on the right has six more flowers than the cactus on the left. How many flowers are on the back of the right cactus?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-18.prompt: The $4\times 4$ grid with one small square missing, shown in the picture, was divided into three equal pieces. Which of the following figures is one of these pieces?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-19.prompt: On a standard die the numbers of dots on opposite faces add up to 7. The die is placed on the first square as shown in the figure and then rolled along the squares as shown by the arrows. When the die reaches the last square, what is the product of the numbers of dots on the two coloured vertical faces?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-20.prompt: Five friends spent their vacation together. In a conversation Adam said: "Yesterday was Wednesday." Beto said: "Tomorrow will be Friday." Carlos said: "The day before yesterday was Tuesday." David said: "The day after tomorrow is Saturday." Finally Eli said: "Today is Monday." One of them was wrong. Who was wrong?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-21.prompt: The teacher wrote the numbers 1 to 8 on the board. Then he covered the numbers with triangles, squares and a circle, as shown. The sum of the numbers covered by the triangles equals the sum of the numbers covered by the squares, and the number covered by the circle is a quarter of that sum. What is the sum of the numbers covered by the triangles and the circle?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-22.prompt: Joana has several sheets of paper with a drawing of a parrot. She wants to paint only the head, the tail and the wing of each parrot, using red, blue or green. The head and tail may have the same colour, but the wing may not have the same colour as the head or the tail. How many sheets can she paint so that no two parrots are painted the same way?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-23.prompt: Jonas and Elias went to the beach on vacation, where they had ice cream every day. Each ice cream had two or three scoops. By the last day of vacation, Jonas and Elias had eaten 23 and 19 scoops, respectively. At least how many days were they on vacation?

kangaroo-at-2020-ecolier-24.prompt: The Kangaroo Hotel has 30 floors numbered 1 to 30, and each floor has 20 rooms numbered 1 to 20. The code to enter a room is made by writing the floor number followed by the room number. But a code can be confusing, as shown in the picture (111 could be floor 1, room 11 or floor 11, room 1). The code 101 is not confusing: it can only mean floor 10, room 1, because floor 1, room 1 has the code 11. How many codes are confusing, including the one in the picture?
